customer_question: Our order didn't include compliance folder creation -- who's responsible for that, and what should we use to build it ourselves?
question_variants: Do we need to create our own compliance folder since it wasn't part of this order?
What should we reference to build a compliance folder ourselves?
How long do we need to keep our self-created compliance folder?
actual_issue: The customer's order for these registrations did not include compliance folder creation as part of the service, and it needed to be clarified that the customer (as Listing Owner) was responsible for assembling their own compliance folder and what they should reference to do so correctly.
plain_english_explanation: The compliance folder isn't automatically included with every registration order -- it has to be purchased as part of the service, or the customer ends up responsible for building it themselves. If it wasn't included, the company that owns the registration needs to put it together on their own, following Bluetooth SIG's own official rules for what the folder should contain, and then hold onto it for the usual length of time in case of an audit.
consultant_answer: Three registration confirmation documents were finalized, with the completed registrations' SDoC (Supplier's Declaration of Conformity) documents downloaded and provided as proof of completion, along with links to each registration's detail page (viewable by the Listing Owner even before the public disclosure date). Since this particular order did not include compliance folder creation, the customer (as Listing Owner) needs to assemble it themselves, following the requirements in Bluetooth SIG's own QPRDv3 specification, section '3.4.1 Compliance Folder,' and retain it until one year after the end of sales of the products listed in each registration's Product List, so it can be presented if Bluetooth SIG conducts an audit.
decision_logic: When an engagement's scope does not include compliance folder creation, responsibility for assembling it falls to the customer as Listing Owner, who should be directed to Bluetooth SIG's own QPRDv3 specification (section 3.4.1, 'Compliance Folder') to ensure it meets the required content and retention standard, rather than assuming a compliance folder will be provided as part of the deliverables.
final_recommendation: When an order does not include compliance folder creation, clearly inform the customer that they are responsible for assembling their own folder, point them to QPRDv3 section 3.4.1 for the requirements, and remind them of the standard one-year post-end-of-sales retention period for SIG audit purposes.
risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming a compliance folder will be automatically provided when it was not included in the order's scope would leave the customer without the documentation required to respond to a future Bluetooth SIG audit.
